title: Dan Hoard Interviews Bryan Cook
text: We are off the field and on the spot with safety Brian Cook, who I first met seven years ago, the last time you came home from Howard University to the University of Cincinnati, that worked out incredibly well for you and you got a feeling for what it was like to play in front of friends and family. Did that have an impact on your choice to come back as a free agent and play for the Bengals? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, absolutely. You know, opportunity to play in front of your loved ones is always a blessing. Um, I did it at the collegiic level, you know, playing for UC. Um, and then now professional level, um, I think, you know, things a little bit, it the stakes a little higher. Um, I say because, you know, I came back home now. I'm married with two kids. So, you know, having the opportunity for my family, um, that I'm creating to experience the family that I was born in um, and came from, it's a remarkable opportunity for me. But not only that, my lady, she's um, she's from Jersey. So having her uh be able to see her family too was a blessing. So it was a right fit. Um I mean at the same time, you know, with that being said, like the organization, you know, obviously they made it a priority to come get me. So, you know, I can't that was a obviously I'd be dumb to say no. You know what I'm saying? So it was a I'm very excited, very um um I can't put into words. I'm ready to get to work for sure. >> What's the best part about being home? free babysitting, the familiarity of knowing where you're going. What is it? >> Uh, I mean, a little bit of everything, honestly. Um, I mean, I got grippo now. I can eat grios when I want to. Um, but yeah, n to it's mainly everything, you know, the family. Um, so we very family oriented, so on both sides. So, um, being able to see our family whenever, you know, we we wish or, you know, having cookouts, things like that that we wasn't able to get before. for I guess u not only made our relationship stronger but at the same time it made you know us uh being parents kind of um take a take a breath for a second okay we not you know we're not we're doing the right thing we we figuring things out um but we realize this how important family is and then now being here to provide and to to help out my family as well as play in front of them you know at a hometown it's man literally I couldn't as a kid I couldn't dream this far be honest with you So >> when you played at UC, they really tried to play up that hometown angle for all of the guys that were from Cincinnati, but is there something to that? Does it feel differently to play for your hometown NFL team? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Um I can't I can't even find the words right now. I'm still like in awe of it. Um but yeah, it's a it's a different type of feeling. It's it's just something that I couldn't I couldn't fathom. I couldn't ask God for cuz I wouldn't even know where to start. Um but it be moments that little things that kind of catch me on guard like me driving to the facility in the morning. It's just like yeah it get a little emotional cuz like bro I grew up 15 minutes from here um my entire life and then being able to say not only say like hey mom I made it but I made it and I'm back home to you know you know show everybody that hey this is this can be done. You know what I'm saying? not just in this level, but any level, you know, just bringing inspiration to the family. Um, and someone to kind of lean on in times of need or thunderstorm and stuff like that. Um, it's always a blessing to be in a position, but I know it comes with a lot a lot of responsibility. But that being said, I'm very thankful and grateful for the opportunity to even do this because like I said, if you would have told me at 8 years old be sitting talking to you from my hometown, it's bro, I would have told you you're crazy. You you mentioned the Bengals coming after you in free agency. You were the first guy they signed this year. It happened on the first day of free agency. Did you know that they were going to pursue you the way that they did or did you think that they were going to? >> No. I mean, not really. I mean, I have, you know, family members that I mean, obviously they're, you know, die hard fan and um every year they would say the same thing. They gonna come get you. I'm like, yeah, we'll see. We'll see. Um but yeah, no. And then once the season broke and and uh things started kind of clearing up, it made sense. And then it wasn't finalized until he actually called me. I was like, "Oh, okay. Okay. Everybody's serious." You know what I'm saying? So, it was nice opportunity I got to come here and play for my hometown. Um but yeah, man. I'm just very grateful for the opportunity. Like, I can't I'm trying to contain myself, but I'm very very grateful. I said, "Y helping a young kid from this area to live out his dreams, and this is beyond what I can dream of." So very grateful. >> Joe Burrow did a news conference recently and he was asked the question, "What do you think of the offseason additions and the first name he mentioned was yours?" He mentioned Dexter Lawrence second, you were first. Uh later he went on to talk about your leadership and the impact that you're having not only on the defense but on the entire team. I know you've heard it or heard about those comments since. >> Yeah. >> What's it mean to you when that guy singles you out as a key addition this off season? >> I mean it means a lot you know I mean when you know apprec uh being appreciated it goes a long way. I mean on you know whether it go to even simpler terms like people e being married or you know have significant others like appreciation goes a long way and so then when I you know come into the building and you know the face of the team it's saying like hey like singling me out as far as like hey you know we excited to have them things like that and it's yeah it pitch a different chip should too cuz now it's like hey I'm doing this not just for myself but for the guys that believe in me in this locker room you know what I'm saying so you want to succeed not just for me but for them Um and so it does go a long way. It goes a long way in numerous different ways. Um you said having a leader be able to speak out um and give you something to not just live up to um for that matter, but more just a sense of um I don't even say security, a sense of just like hey we we behind you, you know, we we have your back. And I said that that feels that feels good. That feels real good. And then so then when I go out there on the field, I know that I'm not just doing it myself, I'm doing it to them. And they understand that and they appreciate that. I think that's what it goes down to. Um but then looking at it from my other side, it's like, bro, I mean, you know, my city has been behind him the whole entire time as well. So it's nice that we can collab and now should I do something that, you know, we had never never been done before. So man, it's a it's a it's a long journey. Um it's a great start. I appreciate for Joe Bro saying the nice things. you know, he's definitely, you know, top top QB in the league um for years. I mean, even when he was hurt, he still came back from injury and and dicing him up and things like that. And I mean, his touchdowns as far as, you know, things like that or even the yards, like numbers don't really give him too much credit because I know he had the injuries, but at the same time, despite his injuries, the numbers he put up is still remarkable. So now be on other side, you know, be able to help him, you know, achieve something that he wants to do. I mean, obviously I want to do it, too, but him and the organization wants to do and achieve and to be able to say I helped. Man, it's it's it's a great feeling. >> Similar to Joe's comments, you were miked up at practice this week. >> And we heard Barrett Carter say, "There's no safety. We would have rather added to this family >> than be Cook." >> Is it a family already? Do you feel that? >> It's a family. It's a family. um you know just coming in and you know guys that don't know me from you know anywhere else but how they interact you know how they ask questions or just you know um listening or even kind of me with their problems I know it's kind of you know crazy to say but you know it takes uh especially for men you know I want take some time as far as um awareness mental awareness you know for um for men to speak out but guys in locker room they able to speak to me you know they they have questions I'm willing to share share my story or you know I try to help him out too. So it goes beyond just a like you know people have lives, people have things they go through and for me being here just in a short amount of time I have people come to me and have you know heartto-he heart conversations and for me that means a lot cuz like you trust me with the information to tell me um and then I'm hoping I can give you the right not saying guidance um but just like hey like you know p perspective to think about um but that's what builds family you know that's just builds connection and chemistry and so then on the field I don't have to worry about what you thinking. Like I know what you're going through at home. I know I know what I know why you're here. Um and it helps me even play better too cuz now I want to make sure that hey your issues I'm helping with your issues by helping you perform or helping us as a team perform well on this field cuz ultimately you know at the end of the day like that's what we here to do. But you know life is tough. Life is hard. Um but yeah it's definitely a family man. Like the love and the and the camaraderie that we have early on like we've been what has it been three three four weeks now? Maybe a month. Um, I haven't seen nothing like it, you know. Um, and I go on my fifth year now. But, man, it's love all around the building and I'm I'm very excited to be a part of part of here, you know, part of home. So, it just everything coming full circle. So, I'm definitely appreciative. But, yeah, family goes, honestly, family is an underrated term, I would say, but it's it's much more than that. And so, I haven't even we haven't even seen the most of it just yet. So, we'll see how that goes. But, yeah, definitely a family for sure. When you were at UC, you were first team all conference. You were on at least one all-American team, but S Gardner was there. Kobe Bryant was there. They had been there longer. They were in the spotlight much more than you were. That's changed now. The spotlight is on you. >> Do you feel that? And do you like it? >> Uh, I mean, do I feel it? Yeah. Do I like it? And it comes with the the territory. Um, ultimately though, you play ball. you know, at the end of the day, the cameras are nice, but it's not going to stop me from doing what I came here to do at the end of the day. I mean, at this point, it's just more just like if I get the chance to watch it, you know, um I'm not doing it for anyone else besides my family. Um and trying to honor God with everything I do.
